returns_to.condition: When the selected development approach does not match uncertainty, risk, participation needs, or legitimacy requirements
When the standard appears justified but phases, testing, infrastructure, roles, decision rights, or release logic are not ready
When the work is technically ready but lacks sufficient consent, authorization, commitment, or recorded conditions for progression
When the intended change is unclear, objectives conflict, or the proposed standard no longer plausibly supports the stated aim
When the problem/opportunity remains vague, competing frames are unresolved, or new evidence contradicts the original framing
When participation is too narrow, representation gaps are material, or there are no credible shapers/testers/early adopters
When scope is too broad, too vague, or the essential feature set is not yet distinguishable from optional work
When reuse, extension, interoperability, or “use something else” questions remain unresolved
When the causal pathway is weak, assumptions are doing too much work, or the standard’s expected mechanism of change is unclear
When the maintenance burden, stewardship model, funding assumptions, adopter cost, or continuity plan are not credible
When important actors, relationships, infrastructure, standards, control points, or dependencies are still poorly understood
